summary: A Shopify app authenticates to the GraphQL Admin API with an access token obtained after a merchant installs the app and approves its scopes; the CLI and app templates handle most of the OAuth flow for you. Building and testing is quick, but a public app distributed through the Shopify App Store goes through a Partner Program setup and an app review, and features that read customer personal data need a separate protected-customer-data approval.

oauthAvailability.note: Apps get an Admin API access token after a merchant install. Shopify CLI handles the OAuth token flow.
alternatives: Custom app with a directly requested token for stores in your own organization

difficulty.reason: Public distribution requires Partner Program setup, app review, and separate protected-customer-data approval.

approvalWait.note: App Store review plus any protected-customer-data approval.

timeEstimate.criticalPath: App Store review (and protected customer data approval for public apps) dominates the timeline.

review.requiredWhen: Required to distribute a public app in the Shopify App Store. Custom apps for your own organization's stores skip the store review.

stages.name: Partner Program setup
stages.description: Create a Partner account and app, configure scopes and the OAuth redirect, and prepare the listing.

stages.name: App Store review
stages.description: Shopify reviews functionality, UX, security, and listing quality before approving the public app.

stages.name: Protected customer data approval
stages.description: Separate approval for public apps whose features read a customer's personal data.

prerequisites.detail: Public apps are created and managed from the Partner Dashboard.
Install and test the OAuth flow on a dev store before submitting.
The CLI and app templates implement the token flow so you rarely hand-code OAuth.

steps.title: Create the app and declare access scopes
steps.detail: Scaffold the app with Shopify CLI (or create it in the Partner Dashboard) and declare the access scopes your features require.

steps.title: Install to a dev store and obtain a token
steps.detail: Run the install flow: the merchant approves the scopes and your app receives an access token (offline by default, online if requested). Send it in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header on every Admin API request.
steps.gotcha: An online access token is further narrowed to the authorizing staff member's permissions, so a request can be refused even when the app holds the scope.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access if needed
steps.detail: If your public app reads a customer's personal data (name, address, phone, email), request protected customer data access; a custom app has it automatically.

steps.title: Prepare the listing and submit for App Store review
steps.detail: Follow the App Store best practices for listing quality, onboarding, and performance, then submit the public app for review.

notes: The OAuth redirect (allowed redirection) URL is configured in the app setup; the CLI manages it in development.
Embedded apps validate an ID token and then exchange it for an access token rather than a classic redirect.

sensitive.consequence: Reading customer personal data requires separate protected customer data approval for public apps.
Access to orders older than 60 days is granted per-app by Shopify, not to every app that declares it.

notes: Some scopes are granted by Shopify to individual apps rather than to every app that declares them.
Offline tokens persist across sessions; online tokens last only as long as the staff session.

blockers.title: App Store submission rejected
blockers.symptom: Shopify declines the public app during review.
blockers.cause: Functionality, UX, security, or listing quality did not meet App Store requirements.
blockers.resolution: Address the reviewer feedback against the App Store best practices and resubmit.

blockers.title: Customer-data fields return empty or error
blockers.symptom: Customer name/email/address fields are missing in responses.
blockers.cause: The public app lacks protected customer data approval, or the plan limits an admin-created custom app's access.
blockers.resolution: Request protected customer data access; for custom apps, verify the store plan's field access.

blockers.title: Online-token request refused despite holding the scope
blockers.symptom: A GraphQL request is refused even though the app declared the scope.
blockers.cause: An online access token is narrowed to the authorizing staff member's permissions.
blockers.resolution: Use an offline token for background work, or ensure the staff member has the needed permission.

agentCan: Scaffold the app with Shopify CLI and wire the token flow
Declare scopes and implement Admin API calls with the access token
Draft the listing copy and best-practices checklist
humanMust: Create and own the Partner account and app
Request protected customer data access and submit for App Store review
handoffPoints: Agent builds and tests the app on a dev store; a human drives Partner setup and the App Store review.

difficulty.note: Public distribution requires review plus protected-customer-data approval.

timeEstimate.note: Review durations are community-reported; Shopify does not publish fixed SLAs.

review.note: Review is required for public apps; stage durations are community-reported.
